justice: Cars parked directly on the pedestrian sidewalks create severe physical obstacles, restricting accessibility for wheelchair users.
The complete absence of tactile paving on the footpaths reduces fairness for visually impaired individuals navigating the space.
High, abrupt curbs on the right side without consistent, dedicated pedestrian ramps limit equitable movement for older adults and persons with disabilities.
safety: The lack of dedicated bike lanes forces cyclists into shared, unmarked road space with motor vehicles, significantly lowering safety.
Haphazardly parked vehicles on pedestrian paths create blind spots and force pedestrians into the active roadway, threatening physical safety.
The wide, straight road lacks any visible traffic calming measures (such as speed bumps or chicanes), posing crossing risks to vulnerable groups like teenagers and the elderly.
livability: Ground-floor commercial shops (e.g., hardware and convenience stores) provide essential daily services, supporting independent living for older adults.
Active storefronts provide passive social surveillance ('eyes on the street'), enhancing the perceived security of the neighborhood for adolescents.
The total lack of public benches or gathering spaces prevents older adults from socializing and utilizing the street as a community space.
sustainability: The complete absence of street trees and vegetation indicates a profound lack of urban green infrastructure and biodiversity support.
Lack of visible public transit infrastructure or dedicated cycling lanes fails to encourage low-carbon transportation options.
Extensive, continuous impermeable concrete and asphalt surfaces without any visible rain gardens or infiltration features exacerbate surface runoff.
aesthetics: The visual environment is overly harsh and barren due to the total lack of street trees, planting strips, or landscaping elements.
Irregularly parked cars scattered across both the roadway and sidewalks create significant visual clutter.
Faded building facades and mismatched, uncoordinated commercial signage contribute to a chaotic and unappealing visual coherence.
comfort: The complete lack of tree canopy or building awnings leaves pedestrians fully exposed to the sun, severely reducing thermal comfort for the elderly during hot weather.
The absence of benches or resting facilities negatively impacts the physical comfort of older adults and disabled pedestrians who require frequent resting intervals.
The wide, barren expanse of pavement combined with encroaching vehicles severely diminishes psychological comfort, making the environment feel highly vehicle-dominated.
walkability: Sidewalk continuity is frequently disrupted by parked motor vehicles, actively forcing pedestrians to walk in the main vehicular right-of-way.
The lack of painted crosswalks, pedestrian islands, or traffic signals makes traversing the wide street intimidating and difficult for older adults.
The absence of street-level shade and resting points makes the walking route physically demanding and unattractive for daily use.
bikeability: The absence of any painted or physically protected bike lanes drastically reduces the feasibility and perceived safety of cycling for all road users.
Cars parked haphazardly along the road edges and curbs force cyclists to merge into the center of the driving lane, increasing the risk of conflict.
There are no visible bicycle parking racks near the commercial storefronts, substantially reducing cycling convenience for running local errands.
